description: Convert a text-based PDF to markdown, preserving headings, lists, links and tables. Returns nothing for a scanned document — call pdf::classify first. Responses are capped; pass max_chars 0 to take the whole document, or pages to take a slice of it.

Profile.description: How faithful the markdown should be to the source characters.

oneOf.description: Preserve the source text as written.
Prefer shorter output, collapsing runs like the dot leaders in a table of contents. Not character-faithful to the source.

request_schema.description: Where the PDF comes from. Exactly one of the two fields must be set.

bytes_base64.description: Base64-encoded PDF bytes, for a document with no path. Mutually exclusive with `path`.

include_images.description: Include `[Image: …]` placeholders. Off by default: nothing here decodes pixels, so a placeholder adds noise without adding information.

max_chars.description: Characters to return before truncating. Omit for the configured default; `0` returns the whole document.

pages.description: 1-indexed pages to convert. Omit for the whole document. A page filter is the cheap way to read a long report: take the pages you need rather than the whole thing truncated.

password.description: Password for an encrypted document. Never logged or echoed back.

path.description: Filesystem path to the PDF. Mutually exclusive with `bytes_base64`.

per_page.description: Return markdown per page as well as the joined document. Useful when a caller wants to route some pages to OCR and keep the rest.

strip_headers_footers.description: Strip repeated running headers and footers.

request_schema.title: Request

Body.description:
A body that may have been shortened to fit one response, and the numbers a caller needs to decide what to do about it.

The cap is what keeps a long document from flooding a model's context. A caller that genuinely wants the whole thing asks for `max_chars: 0`, which is the shape a worker-to-worker pipeline uses to move a document without it passing through anyone's context.

preview.description: Leading characters of the content. Present only when the body was truncated, so a caller can see the shape of what it did not get without re-reading the start of `text`.

text.description: The content, shortened to the effective character cap.

total_chars.description: Characters the document actually holds. Equal to `chars` when nothing was dropped.

truncated.description: `true` when `text` stops short of the document. Ask again with a page filter, or with `max_chars: 0` to take everything.

DocumentType.description: What a document is made of.

oneOf.description: Pictures of pages. Every page needs OCR.
Images with little or no text layer.
Some pages carry text, others do not. Read `pages_needing_ocr`.

PageOcrReason.description: Why one page cannot be read without OCR.

reasons.description: Machine-readable reasons: `scanned` (a raster page), `no_text` (nothing extractable and nothing to OCR), `vector_text` (characters drawn as outlines rather than text) or `suspected_garbled_text` (a text layer that decodes to nonsense).

PageResult.description: One page of markdown, with its own OCR verdict.

needs_ocr.description: `true` when this page's text is not trustworthy and OCR would do better.

ocr_reason.description: Machine-readable reason, when the cause is known.

document_type.description: The document-level verdict, so a caller that skipped `pdf::classify` still learns it got nothing because the document is a scan.

has_encoding_issues.description: `true` when font encodings decoded badly. The markdown, if any, is not to be trusted.

pages_converted.description: Pages actually converted. Equal to `page_count` unless `pages` was set.

pages_with_columns.description: 1-indexed pages laid out in multiple columns.

source.description: Source label: the file name, or `<inline>` for an in-memory document.
